Chapter 1 · 第一章

The Role of a Tech Lead技术负责人这一角色

— PDF p.17 —

The tech lead role is one of the most misunderstood positions in the tech industry. It’s a role that exists at the intersection of people, technology, and business, and yet there’s little consensus on what it actually means. This lack of clarity often leaves new tech leads feeling unsure about what’s expected of them and how to approach the role effectively.

技术负责人（tech lead）是科技行业里最被误解的职位之一。它处在人、技术与业务三者的交汇点上，然而对于它究竟意味着什么，业界却鲜有共识。这种模糊不清常常让新任技术负责人感到茫然，不清楚公司对自己的期望是什么，也不知道该如何有效地胜任这个角色。

Every company seems to have its own version of the tech lead role, shaped by their culture, processes, and priorities. Some see the role as deeply technical, while others focus heavily on team dynamics and processes. Understanding these differences and defining what it means within your specific context is the first step to succeeding as a tech lead.

每家公司似乎都有自己版本的技术负责人角色，由其文化、流程和优先级塑造。有的把它看得非常技术化，有的则高度关注团队协作与流程。理解这些差异，并在你自己的具体情境中定义这个角色意味着什么，是你成功担任技术负责人的第一步。

That’s why, in this chapter, I’ll outline the essential aspects of the tech lead role to help you understand what to expect and how to approach it. I’ll begin by defining what a tech lead is, including the scope and daily responsibilities. Then, I’ll explore how to make sense of the expectations placed on you, whether you have a formal job description or not, and offer guidance on evaluating whether this role is right for you.

正因如此，在本章中，我会梳理技术负责人角色的核心要点，帮你了解可以期待什么、又该如何着手。我会先定义技术负责人是什么，包括其职责范围与日常工作；然后探讨如何理解加诸于你身上的各种期望——无论你是否有一份正式的岗位说明书；并就如何判断这个角色是否适合你给出指导。

I’ll also look at the different paths people take to become a tech lead, from transitioning within your current team to forming entirely new ones. Finally, I’ll cover the critical skills and mindset shifts you’ll need to go through in this transition.

我还会看看人们成为技术负责人所走的不同路径——从在现有团队中接任，到从零组建全新团队。最后，我会讨论在这一转变中你所需完成的关键技能与心态转变。

— PDF p.18 —

What Is a Tech Lead?什么是技术负责人？

When I ask tech leads, “What’s expected of you?” the responses are wildly different, covering a wide range of skills and responsibilities.

当我问技术负责人“公司对你的期望是什么？”时，得到的回答千差万别，涵盖了五花八门的技能与职责。

At one extreme, some describe the tech lead as the most technical person on the team, someone with deep expertise in the tech stack who makes all the decisions and contributes code daily, often at the same level as any other engineer. The role is seen as highly hands-on, deeply technical, and rooted in direct contributions to the team’s output.

在一个极端，有人把技术负责人描述为团队里技术最强的人：对技术栈有深厚专长，包揽所有决策，每天都写代码，产出水平与其他工程师不相上下。这个角色被看作高度亲力亲为、深扎技术、直接为团队产出做贡献的位置。

At the other end of the spectrum, the tech lead is described as someone who rarely codes, either due to lack of time or because they deliberately choose to focus on other priorities, like people, processes, and shielding the team from distractions. In this view, the tech lead is more of a facilitator, working closely with the product manager (PM) to manage the backlog and ensure smooth collaboration.

在另一个极端，技术负责人被描述为一个几乎不写代码的人——要么是因为没时间，要么是因为刻意把精力放在别的优先事项上，比如人、流程，以及为团队挡住干扰。在这种视角下，技术负责人更像一个“使能者”（facilitator），与产品经理（PM）紧密合作来管理待办清单（backlog），确保协作顺畅。

Figure 1-1 shows a word cloud compiled from typical responses I get when training groups of tech leads and asking, “What words do you associate with ‘tech lead’?”

图 1-1 是一张词云，它汇总了我在培训技术负责人小组时提出“你会把哪些词和‘技术负责人’联系在一起？”所得到的典型回答。

— PDF p.19 —

These examples show just how varied the expectations can be, from being a hands-on technical expert to focusing entirely on people and processes. The reality is that the tech lead role sits somewhere in the middle, requiring a careful balance between technical leadership, team development, and stakeholder alignment. That balance isn’t fixed. It can shift over time, depending on the maturity of your team, the phase of the project, or even the specific challenges you’re facing.

这些例子说明，外界对这个角色的期望有多宽泛——从一个亲力亲为的技术专家，到完全聚焦于人与流程。现实是，技术负责人这个角色处在两者之间的某个位置，需要在技术领导力、团队发展与利益相关方对齐之间取得精妙的平衡。而这个平衡点并非一成不变：它会随时间推移而移动，取决于团队的成熟度、项目所处的阶段，甚至你当下正面临的具体挑战。

A tech lead is expected to guide the team through decision making, ensuring that everyone’s input is heard and considered, rather than just making decisions unilaterally. This requires a breadth of knowledge, not just about technical areas like infrastructure, architecture, and the tech stack but also about the business context and stakeholder management.

技术负责人要引导团队完成决策过程，确保每个人的意见都被听到、被考虑，而不是单方面拍板。这需要广博的知识——不仅包括基础设施、架构、技术栈等技术领域，还包括业务背景和利益相关方管理。

At the same time, a tech lead must support the team’s delivery while helping individual team members grow. It’s a role that demands both technical expertise and people skills, combining them effectively to build alignment, encourage teamwork, and deliver impactful results.

与此同时，技术负责人既要支撑团队的交付，又要帮助团队成员个人成长。这个角色同时要求技术专长和人际能力，并把两者有效结合起来，以建立共识、鼓励协作、交付有影响力的成果。

This wide range of interpretations of the role can be confusing, especially for new tech leads, but it also highlights why the role is so critical, and why defining it within your context is essential.

对这个角色如此多样的解读会让人困惑，对新任技术负责人尤其如此；但这也恰恰说明为什么这个角色如此关键，以及为什么在你自己的情境中把它定义清楚至关重要。

Defining the Scope界定职责范围

Given how widely the tech lead role can vary, it’s helpful to look at how different experts and industry leaders define it. Each brings a slightly different lens, technical, organizational, or people-focused, reflecting the fluid nature of the role across different companies and team setups.

鉴于技术负责人角色的差异如此之大，看看不同专家和行业领军人物是如何定义它的，会很有启发。每个人都带来一个略有不同的视角——技术的、组织的，或聚焦于人的——这也反映了这个角色在不同公司、不同团队架构下的流动性。

Camille Fournier, in The Manager’s Path (O’Reilly), describes the tech lead as a senior individual contributor who helps a team of engineers work together effectively. She emphasizes coordination, communication, and supporting the team in delivering high-quality work. As she explains it, the tech lead isn’t necessarily the strongest coder but the one ensuring that things move forward smoothly.

Camille Fournier 在《The Manager’s Path》（O’Reilly 出版）一书中，把技术负责人描述为一位资深个人贡献者（senior IC），其职责是帮助一个工程师团队高效协作。她强调协调、沟通，以及支持团队交付高质量的工作。用她的话说，技术负责人未必是代码写得最好的人，而是那个确保事情顺利推进的人。

Will Larson, in Staff Engineer (self-published), presents the tech lead as an archetype of staff-plus roles: “The Tech Lead guides the approach and execution of a particular team. They partner closely with a single manager, but sometimes they partner with two or three managers within a focused area. Some companies

Will Larson 在《Staff Engineer》（自费出版）一书中，把技术负责人描绘成 staff 及以上级别角色的一种原型：“技术负责人指导某个特定团队的方法与执行。他们与一位经理紧密搭档，但有时会在某个聚焦领域内与两三位经理合作。有些公司

— PDF p.20 —

also have a Tech Lead Manager role, which is similar to the Tech Lead archetype but exists on the engineering manager ladder and includes people management responsibilities.” His framing emphasizes the tech lead’s proximity to execution and operational leadership.

还设有‘技术负责人经理’（Tech Lead Manager）这一角色，它与技术负责人原型相似，但处在工程经理的晋升阶梯上，并承担人员管理职责。”他的这一框架强调了技术负责人贴近执行、贴近运营领导的特点。

Pat Kua, in his book Talking with Tech Leads (CreateSpace), defines the role as “a leader, responsible for a (software) development team, who spends at least 30 percent of their time writing code with the team.” His definition underscores the hybrid nature of the role: still technical but with an added layer of responsibility for team effectiveness and communication.

Pat Kua 在其著作《Talking with Tech Leads》（CreateSpace 出版）中，把这个角色定义为“一位负责（软件）开发团队的领导者，其至少 30% 的时间要与团队一起写代码”。他的定义凸显了这个角色的混合属性：仍然是技术的，但额外多了一层对团队效能和沟通的责任。

Pat’s work had a lasting influence on how I approached the role early in my career. One of my first tech lead trainings was with him, back when we were both at Thoughtworks, and many of the lessons from that experience continue to shape how I teach and support tech leads today.

Pat 的著作对我职业生涯早期如何胜任这个角色产生了深远影响。我参加的最早一批技术负责人培训就是跟他一起上的，那时我们都在 Thoughtworks；那段经历中的许多教训，至今仍在塑造我如今教授和支持技术负责人的方式。

These perspectives highlight different, but overlapping, facets of the tech lead role: from deep technical execution to team coordination and stakeholder alignment. And that diversity reflects what I’ve consistently observed in practice.

这些观点凸显了技术负责人角色中不同却又相互重叠的侧面：从深度技术执行，到团队协调，再到利益相关方对齐。而这种多样性，也正反映了我在实践中反复观察到的现象。

Drawing from my own experience as a tech lead, and from training hundreds of tech leads over the years, I’ve seen this role take shape in many forms. The tech leads I’ve worked with have come from a wide range of environments: product companies and consultancies, startups and large enterprises, and teams at varying levels of maturity. This includes fintech, ecommerce, and SaaS (software as a service) organizations; agile and less agile teams; both layered and flat hierarchies; and setups ranging from internal tooling to customer-facing product teams.

从我自己做技术负责人的经历，以及这些年培训数百位技术负责人的经验来看，我见过这个角色呈现出许多不同的形态。与我共事过的技术负责人来自各种各样的环境：产品公司与咨询公司、初创企业与大型企业，以及成熟度各不相同的团队。这其中包括金融科技、电商和 SaaS（软件即服务）类组织；敏捷程度高低不一的团队；层级分明与扁平化的组织架构；以及从内部工具团队到面向客户的产品团队等各种配置。

Based on this broad exposure and firsthand experience, I’ve come to see a clear throughline in what great tech leads do. While the role flexes based on context, there’s a common core. Here’s how I define it:

基于这种广泛接触和亲身体验，我逐渐看到优秀技术负责人身上一条清晰的主线。虽然这个角色会随情境而伸缩，但存在一个共同的内核。下面是我的定义：

The tech lead is a software engineer responsible for leading a development team and accountable for the technical deliverables of that team.

技术负责人是一位软件工程师，负责带领一支开发团队，并对该团队的技术交付成果负责。

Being accountable for technical deliverables also means ensuring that the team’s work aligns with stakeholder expectations. This alignment places the tech lead role right at the intersection of people, business, and technology. It’s a balancing act that requires understanding both the technical and nontechnical aspects of the role, as shown in Figure 1-2.

对技术交付成果负责，也意味着要确保团队的工作与利益相关方的期望保持一致。这种一致性把技术负责人这个角色恰恰放在了人、业务与技术的交汇点上。这是一种平衡之举，需要同时理解这个角色的技术层面与非技术层面，如图 1-2 所示。

— PDF p.21 —

So, to be an effective tech lead, you need to successfully implement several tasks, described in the following sections.

因此，要成为一名高效的技术负责人，你需要成功地落实若干项任务，下面几节将逐一展开。

Build a strong, high-performing team打造一支强大、高绩效的团队

First, you need to focus on building a strong, high-performing team. It took me a while to figure out what that really means, but here’s what I’ve learned: a strong team delivers value consistently. They work together like a well-oiled machine, complementing each other’s skills and continuously growing. They don’t wait to be told what to do; they take initiative, and responsibility is shared across the team.

首先，你需要专注于打造一支强大、高绩效的团队。我花了好一阵子才弄明白这到底意味着什么，以下是我的心得：一支强大的团队会持续不断地交付价值。他们像一台上好了油的机器一样协同运转，彼此技能互补，并持续成长。他们不会等着别人告诉自己该做什么；他们会主动行动，责任由整个团队共同承担。

To build and maintain a team like this, you’ll need to invest time and energy into your people. That means mentoring and coaching them, creating opportunities for growth through delegation, and providing feedback that actually helps them improve. It also means supporting collaboration by addressing conflict, facilitating open conversations, and building strong relationships. It’s challenging work, but it’s worth it. Because without effective collaboration, you don’t have a team; you just have a group of individuals trying to work together. More on this in the section “Building a High-Performing Team” on page 180.

要打造并维持这样一支团队，你需要在“人”身上投入时间和精力。这意味着辅导和训练他们，通过委派任务创造成长机会，并给出真正能帮助他们进步的反馈。这也意味着要通过化解冲突、推动开放对话、建立牢固关系来支持协作。这是充满挑战的工作，但值得去做。因为没有有效的协作，你拥有的就不是一支团队，而只是一群试图凑在一起干活的个人。更多内容参见第 180 页“打造高绩效团队”一节。

But there’s another layer here that’s often overlooked: as a tech lead, you’ll also play a critical role in shaping career growth and performance outcomes for your team. While you might not be the one making final decisions on things like promotions or compensation, your input carries weight, especially during performance review cycles.

但这里还有一个常被忽视的层面：作为技术负责人，你还将在塑造团队成员的职业成长与绩效结果方面发挥关键作用。虽然晋升、薪酬这类事情的最终决定可能不由你做，但你的意见是有分量的——尤其是在绩效评估周期里。

— PDF p.22 —

Your role in performance reviews and career development can vary widely depending on your company’s structure and culture. In some organizations, tech leads are deeply involved in performance review cycles, mentoring team members toward the next level, providing structured feedback, and partnering closely with engineering managers to support individual growth. In others, tech leads are barely involved at all, as the expectation is that team leads or engineering managers will take care of the heavy lifting when it comes to reviews and development.

你在绩效评估与职业发展中扮演的角色，会因公司的组织结构和文化而大相径庭。在有些组织里，技术负责人深度参与绩效评估周期，辅导团队成员迈向更高职级，给出结构化的反馈，并与工程经理紧密合作、支持个人成长。而在另一些公司，技术负责人几乎不参与其中——因为大家默认团队负责人或工程经理会把评估与发展这些重活扛下来。

Still, even in companies where your formal involvement is limited, your perspective and feedback are often sought, especially when it comes to evaluating technical growth, impact, and readiness for more responsibility. In many cases, your input may also be requested for engineers outside your team, particularly when you’ve collaborated on cross-functional work. Promotion cycles can be intense, and tech leads often find themselves at the center of them, writing feedback, assessing performance, and advocating for the people they work with every day.

不过，即便在你正式参与程度有限的公司，大家也常常会征求你的看法和反馈，尤其是在评估技术成长、影响力，以及是否能承担更多责任的时候。很多时候，你的意见还会被征求给团队之外的工程师，尤其是在你们合作过跨职能项目之后。晋升周期往往十分紧张，技术负责人常常发现自己正处在旋涡中心：写反馈、评估绩效，为与自己朝夕相处的同事发声。

For a deeper dive into this part of the role, including how to navigate performance reviews, see the section “How to Approach Performance Reviews” on page 197.

想更深入地了解这个角色的这一面（包括如何应对绩效评估），参见第 197 页“如何应对绩效评估”一节。

Lead technical topics主导技术议题

As a tech lead, you need to ensure your team can deliver on expectations and handle any technical challenges thrown their way. But this doesn’t mean you need to be the most technical person on the team or take on every technical decision, code review, or pull request yourself.

作为技术负责人，你需要确保团队能够兑现期望、应对抛到他们面前的任何技术挑战。但这并不意味着你必须是团队里技术最强的人，也不意味着每一个技术决策、每一次代码评审、每一个合并请求（PR）都要你亲自上手。

A strong technical background is certainly important, and some familiarity with the technologies your team uses is definitely helpful. However, you don’t need to have deep expertise in every part of the tech stack. What’s important is having enough knowledge to code alongside your team when necessary, staying informed about code changes, and effectively troubleshooting issues that arise. This foundation allows you to guide your team in building a technical strategy, making informed decisions, and solving production problems.

扎实的技术背景当然重要，对团队所用技术有所熟悉也肯定有帮助。然而，你并不需要对技术栈的每一层都有深厚专长。重要的是你拥有足够的知识，能在必要时和团队一起写代码、及时了解代码变更，并有效地排查出现的问题。有了这个基础，你才能引导团队制定技术战略、做出有依据的决策，并解决生产环境中的问题。

The good news is, you don’t need to carry the weight of technical expertise on your own. As a tech lead, you have tools at your disposal to share responsibility and create a balanced workflow. Delegation is key. Delegating tasks to team members who have deeper expertise in certain areas, or who are eager to learn, ensures the workload is distributed effectively while supporting their growth. This approach not only increases your team’s overall technical capabilities but also reinforces collaboration and trust.

好消息是，技术专长这副担子不必你一个人扛。作为技术负责人，你手头有工具可以分担责任、营造平衡的工作流。委派（delegation）是关键。把任务委派给在某些领域更有专长、或渴望学习的团队成员，既能让工作量得到有效分配，又能支持他们成长。这种做法不仅提升了团队整体的技术能力，也强化了协作与信任。

Equally important is ensuring commitment to the technical strategy and the results you aim to achieve. A great way to do this is by facilitating open,

同样重要的是，要确保团队对技术战略和你所追求的结果真正投入。一个很好的做法，是在团队内部主持开放、

— PDF p.23 —

productive conversations within your team. Ensure that everyone has a chance to contribute, share their ideas, and be involved in decision making.

富有成效的对话。确保每个人都有机会贡献意见、分享想法，并参与决策。

I’ve seen this approach work firsthand. I once led a team of six developers to deliver a major feature with high business impact on time, under a tight three-month deadline, despite having limited knowledge of the tech stack and business context, no prior relationships within the company, and multiple dependencies on other teams. Instead of trying to become the technical expert, I leaned on team members with deeper expertise in the technology. My focus was on unblocking the team, addressing pain points like backlog alignment, consistent refinement, knowledge sharing, and creating a process that enabled us to deliver value continuously. By fully utilizing everyone’s skills and providing clarity on what to work on and how to approach tasks, we achieved our goals together.

我亲眼见过这种做法奏效。有一次我带领一支六人开发团队，在三个月的紧张工期内按时交付了一个业务影响很大的重要功能——而当时我对技术栈和业务背景知之有限、在公司里没有任何既有的人脉，还面临对其他团队的多重依赖。我没有试图把自己变成技术专家，而是依靠团队里在该技术上更有专长的成员。我的重点是为团队扫清障碍：解决待办对齐、持续的待办梳理、知识共享等痛点，并建立一套流程让我们能够持续交付价值。通过充分发挥每个人的技能，并把“做什么、怎么做”讲清楚，我们共同达成了目标。

Leading technical topics isn’t about knowing everything or doing everything; it’s about enabling your team to deliver efficiently on expectations.

主导技术议题，不在于你无所不知或事必躬亲；而在于让团队能够高效地兑现期望。

Bridge tech and business架起技术与业务的桥梁

I’d argue this is one of the most important responsibilities you have as a tech lead because it’s something only you can do. You’re the go-to person for your stakeholders, and while other developers on your team can take the lead on technical strategy or mentoring, bridging tech and business isn’t something you can delegate. It’s your job to make your team’s successes visible and proactively communicate potential blockers, risks, or delivery impacts to stakeholders. That includes translating technical decisions, like technical debt, refactoring needs, or scaling constraints, into terms that make sense to nontechnical partners.

我认为这是你作为技术负责人最重要的职责之一，因为这件事只有你能做。你是利益相关方的首选对接人；虽然团队里其他开发可以牵头技术战略或辅导新人，但架起技术与业务之间的桥梁这件事，你无法委派别人。你的职责是让团队的成功被看见，并主动向利益相关方通报潜在的阻塞、风险或对交付的影响。这包括把技术决策——比如技术债、重构需求、扩容上的约束——翻译成非技术伙伴能听懂的语言。

To do this well, you need to constantly invest in building relationships with your team’s stakeholders, rather than just waiting for them to come to you. Set up regular one-on-ones, progress updates, or tracking processes to provide visibility into your team’s work. I have seen too many tech leads suffering because they overlooked this, forgetting how much these relationships can influence your team’s direction and your ability to lead effectively.

要做好这件事，你需要持续投入，主动与团队的利益相关方建立关系，而不是坐等他们找上门来。建立定期的一对一沟通、进展同步或跟踪机制，让团队的工作透明可见。我见过太多技术负责人因为忽视这一点而吃苦头——他们忘了这些关系对你团队的方向、以及你能否有效领导，有着多大的影响力。

Your role doesn’t stop there. You’re also responsible for bringing back any relevant information to your team, whether it’s feedback, shifting priorities, or risks. And when needed, you have to shield your team from external pressures that might disrupt their focus or morale. This balance between keeping stakeholders informed and protecting your team ensures everyone stays aligned and focused. It’s a fine line, but when done right, it can make a huge difference in how your team performs and how smoothly everything runs.

你的角色还不止于此。你还负责把相关信息带回到团队——无论是反馈、优先级的变化，还是风险。在需要的时候，你还得为团队挡住那些可能扰乱他们专注度或士气的外部压力。在“让利益相关方知情”与“保护团队”之间取得平衡，才能确保大家既对齐又专注。这是一条微妙的界限，但一旦拿捏得当，就会让团队的表现和整体运转的顺畅度大不一样。

— PDF p.24 —

By balancing these three core responsibilities, building a strong team, leading technical topics, and bridging tech with business, you’re setting your team up for success. Each of these areas demands attention and focus, as they are all interconnected. A high-performing team requires a clear technical strategy and alignment with business goals. There is no way around it.

通过平衡这三项核心职责——打造强大团队、主导技术议题、架起技术与业务的桥梁——你就在为团队的成功铺路。这三个方面都需要你投入关注与精力，因为它们彼此关联。一支高绩效团队，离不开清晰的技术战略，也离不开与业务目标的对齐。这一点没有捷径可走。

Tech Lead versus Team Lead versus Lead Developer versus Engineering Manager技术负责人 vs 团队负责人 vs 首席开发 vs 工程经理

Throughout the writing of this book, I received a lot of feedback questioning whether I was actually describing a team lead, a lead developer, or even an engineering manager (EM). The confusion is completely justified.

在写这本书的整个过程中，我收到大量反馈，质疑我描述的到底是团队负责人（team lead）、首席开发（lead developer），甚至是工程经理（EM）。这种困惑完全是有道理的。

Different companies define these roles differently. Titles are often inconsistent, and responsibilities are distributed in ways that reflect the company’s size, culture, and maturity. But after playing this role with different clients, as well as training and coaching over 300 tech leads from companies of all shapes and sizes over the past three years, I keep coming to the same conclusion:

不同公司对这些角色的定义各不相同。头衔常常前后不一，职责的划分方式也反映了公司的规模、文化与成熟度。但在为不同客户扮演过这个角色、并在过去三年里培训和辅导了 300 多位来自各种规模公司的技术负责人之后，我反复得出同一个结论：

The tech lead role is a people management role.

技术负责人这个角色，本质上是一个人员管理的角色。

Even if the job description doesn’t say so. Even if it doesn’t sound like it. Even if some techies don’t like it.

哪怕岗位说明书上没这么写。哪怕听起来不像。哪怕有些技术人不愿听到这话。

Because while tech is the first word in the title, it’s the word lead that truly defines the role.

因为尽管“技术（tech）”是头衔里的第一个词，但真正定义这个角色的，是“负责人（lead）”这个词。

Anyone who has stepped into the tech lead position quickly realizes that the job involves far more people-related work than they expected. I’ve heard many say:

任何真正走上技术负责人岗位的人，都会很快意识到这份工作涉及的与人相关的事务，远比他们预想的多得多。我听过很多人这样说：

“This role is way more people-focused than I thought.”

“这个角色比我想象的要‘人’得多。”

“This is not what I signed up for.”

“这可不是我当初报名想做的事。”

“I don’t want to be responsible for people’s growth.”

“我不想为别人的成长负责。”

The reality is that even if a tech lead is officially responsible only for delivery, product quality, and technical decision making, these responsibilities are impossible to fulfill without managing people effectively. How do you ensure quality and delivery without regular check-ins? How do you grow technical excellence without giving feedback, resolving conflict, and motivating others?

现实是，哪怕一位技术负责人在官方上只对交付、产品质量和技术决策负责，若不能有效地管理人，这些职责也根本无从履行。没有定期的沟通跟进，你如何保证质量和交付？不给予反馈、不化解冲突、不激励他人，你又如何培育技术上的卓越？

So, let’s clear up some common misunderstandings that can arise from the various job titles and roles that overlap with being a tech lead.

那么，让我们来澄清一些常见的误解——它们源于与技术负责人相互重叠的各种头衔和角色。

— PDF p.25 —

Tech lead技术负责人

The tech lead is a software engineer who leads a technical team and is accountable for the outcomes of that team. The keyword is accountable. When something breaks or slips, the tech lead is the one who answers for it. That’s why they’re involved in everything that affects those outcomes: planning, delivery, technical guidance, mentoring, stakeholder management, and people growth.

技术负责人是一位软件工程师，带领一支技术团队，并对该团队的结果负责。关键词是“负责（accountable）”。当出了故障或进度延误时，技术负责人就是那个要为此给出交代的人。正因如此，他们会介入一切影响这些结果的事务：规划、交付、技术指导、辅导、利益相关方管理，以及人的成长。

Even if your company doesn’t explicitly define this as people management, it is people management in practice.

哪怕你的公司没有把它明确定义为人员管理，在实践中它就是人员管理。

Tech lead versus team lead技术负责人 vs 团队负责人

The team lead role is often conflated with the tech lead. Traditionally, people think of the tech lead as handling technical direction and the team lead as focusing on people. But in most teams I’ve seen, there isn’t a strict split; it’s the same person doing both jobs under one title called one or the other.

团队负责人（team lead）这个角色常常与技术负责人混为一谈。传统上，人们认为技术负责人负责技术方向，团队负责人聚焦于人。但在我见过的大多数团队里，二者并没有严格的分工；往往是同一个人顶着其中一个头衔，同时干着两份活。

Some companies might formally separate them, but it’s rare to see both roles within a single team. In practice, the difference is mostly semantic. Even if both roles do exist in the same team, it very often happens that they struggle to align due to significant overlap. To avoid stepping on each other’s toes, they need to establish very clear boundaries, and that takes strong communication and alignment skills on both sides.

有些公司可能会在形式上把两者分开，但在同一个团队里同时设这两个角色的情况很少见。实践中，二者的区别大多只是语义上的。即便同一个团队里两个角色都存在，也常常因为职责高度重叠而难以对齐。为了避免互相踩脚，他们需要划定非常清晰的边界，而这对双方的沟通与对齐能力都提出了很高要求。

Tech lead versus lead developer技术负责人 vs 首席开发

The lead developer is a progression from senior developer. The focus is still highly technical, but the impact is broader, usually going beyond the current team. Lead developers drive initiatives, contribute to architecture, and mentor others, often across multiple teams. They might take on responsibilities like chapter lead or security champion, extending their influence without formally leading a team.

首席开发（lead developer）是资深开发（senior developer）的进一步晋升。其关注点仍然高度技术化，但影响力更宽，通常超出当前团队。首席开发会主导各种专项、参与架构设计、辅导他人，而且往往横跨多个团队。他们可能承担诸如技术分会负责人（chapter lead）或安全代言人（security champion）之类的职责，在不正式带领团队的情况下扩大自己的影响力。

In terms of hierarchy, lead developers are often at the same level as tech leads, just with a different scope: where the tech lead is accountable for a single team’s output, the lead developer often works horizontally and is responsible for leading different initiatives, working closely with the tech lead and supporting them in raising the overall technical quality.

在职级上，首席开发往往与技术负责人同级，只是职责范围不同：技术负责人对单一团队的产出负责，而首席开发通常横向铺开，负责领导不同的专项，与技术负责人紧密合作，支持他们提升整体技术质量。

Tech lead versus engineering manager技术负责人 vs 工程经理

The engineering manager (EM) role is another title with highly inconsistent definitions across companies, and it often overlaps with or absorbs responsibilities

工程经理（EM）这个头衔，在不同公司之间的定义同样极不一致，而且它常常与技术负责人的职责相互重叠，甚至直接吞并这些职责

— PDF p.26 —

commonly associated with tech leads. While both roles involve leadership, the nature of that leadership is different.

——即那些通常被归到技术负责人名下的工作。虽然两个角色都涉及领导，但领导的性质并不相同。

Tech leads are deeply embedded in the team, driving technical delivery, mentoring engineers, and ensuring the day-to-day runs smoothly. EMs, on the other hand, tend to operate at a broader level. They often support multiple teams, focus on people development, manage compensation, and shape long-term team health and organizational strategy. In setups where each team has a tech lead, this division works particularly well: the EM supports the tech leads, while the tech leads support the engineers.

技术负责人深度嵌入团队之中，推动技术交付、辅导工程师，确保日常运转顺畅。而工程经理则倾向于在更宏观的层面运作。他们往往同时支持多个团队，聚焦于人的发展，管理薪酬，并塑造团队的长期健康度与组织战略。在每个团队都配有技术负责人的架构下，这种分工尤其顺畅：工程经理支持各位技术负责人，技术负责人则支持各位工程师。

In some organizations, tech leads take on all leadership responsibilities because there are no engineering managers. In others, engineering managers handle both people and technical leadership because there are no designated tech leads. The setup varies greatly, and there’s no one-size-fits-all model, only what works best for the team and the context.

在有些组织里，因为没有工程经理，技术负责人要承担全部领导职责。在另一些组织里，因为没有指定的技术负责人，工程经理则同时扛下人员领导和技术领导。组织架构千差万别，并不存在放之四海而皆准的模式，只有对团队和具体情境而言最有效的那种安排。

I see the EM role as a natural career progression in tech after the tech lead role. You can read more about the EM role and how it compares to the tech lead path in the section “Advancing to Engineering Manager” on page 344.

我把工程经理看作技术负责人之后在技术职业道路上的自然进阶。关于工程经理这个角色以及它与技术负责人路径的对比，可参见第 344 页“晋升为工程经理”一节。

Day-to-Day Responsibilities日常职责

Now that you have a better understanding of a tech lead’s responsibilities, let’s translate them into what a typical day for a tech lead might look like.

既然你对技术负责人的职责已经有了更好的理解，下面我们把这些职责翻译成技术负责人典型的一天可能是什么样子。

Meetings会议

Yes! You’ll be spending a lot of time in meetings. There’s no way around it. No matter how good your async communication skills are, meetings are essential for alignment (standups, plannings, retros, strategy sessions, discoveries), supporting your team (one-on-ones, feedback sessions, addressing conflicts), and staying informed about changes (all-hands meetings).

没错！你会把大量时间花在会议上。这一点躲不掉。无论你的异步沟通能力多强，会议对于对齐（站会、规划会、复盘会、战略会、需求探索会）、支持团队（一对一、反馈面谈、化解冲突）以及及时了解变化（全员大会）都是不可或缺的。

But that doesn’t mean meetings should consume all your time. Over time, you’ll learn which ones truly require your presence, which can be delegated to others, and which can be cut altogether. This allows you to balance your time with two other equally important areas: coding and thinking time.

但这并不意味着会议应当占满你全部时间。随着经验积累，你会逐渐明白哪些会议确实需要你出席、哪些可以委派给别人、哪些干脆可以砍掉。这样你才能把时间与另外两个同样重要的领域做好平衡：写代码，以及思考时间。

Coding写代码

I made the mistake once of staying away from the code for too long, and one day, I jumped back in only to realize I didn’t even recognize it anymore. Trust me, you don’t want to get to that point.

我曾经犯过一个错：离开代码太久。直到有一天我重新扑进去，才发现自己已经完全认不出它了。相信我，你不会希望走到那一步。

— PDF p.27 —

It’s easy as a tech lead to get swept up in meetings and high-level discussions, but staying hands-on, coding alongside your team weekly, makes all the difference. It keeps you connected to the work, helps you stay in tune with code quality, and ensures you’re better equipped to make technical decisions together with the team.

作为技术负责人，你很容易被会议和高层讨论卷走；但坚持亲自动手、每周都和团队一起写代码，效果会大不相同。这能让你与工作保持连接，帮你持续感知代码质量，也让你更有能力与团队一起做出技术决策。

Pairing with team members is another great way to stay close to both the code and the people. It helps you spot issues early and understand how each developer is progressing, and serves as a powerful mentoring tool. Beyond pairing, reviewing others’ code, looking through the codebase, and regularly checking pull requests are also useful ways to stay updated, even if you’re not writing much code yourself.

与团队成员结对编程（pairing），是同时贴近代码和人的又一个好办法。它帮你及早发现问题、了解每位开发的进展，也是一种强有力的辅导工具。除了结对，评审别人的代码、通读代码库、定期查看合并请求，也是保持跟进的有效方式——哪怕你自己写的代码并不多。

And don’t forget about architecture and system design. These are key areas where tech leads are expected to provide guidance and oversight. Staying involved in design discussions keeps your technical context sharp and ensures the team is making aligned, scalable decisions.

还有，别忘了架构与系统设计。这些都是技术负责人理应提供指导和把关的关键领域。持续参与设计讨论，能让你的技术上下文保持敏锐，也能确保团队做出的决策既对齐又可扩展。

Another key area that takes up a surprising amount of time is writing and reviewing technical documentation and plans. Whether you’re drafting a design doc, reviewing an RFC (request for comments), or commenting on a team member proposal, this kind of written work is essential to maintain alignment and drive thoughtful technical decision making. It keeps you connected to the work, helps you stay in tune with code quality, and ensures you’re better equipped to make technical decisions together with the team.

另一个占用时间多得出人意料的关键领域，是撰写和评审技术文档与方案。无论你是在起草设计文档、评审一份 RFC（意见征求稿），还是对团队成员的提案发表评论，这类书面工作对于维持对齐、推动深思熟虑的技术决策都至关重要。它让你与工作保持连接，帮你持续感知代码质量，也让你更有能力与团队一起做出技术决策。

One important thing to mention here is that, as your coding time naturally decreases and your focus becomes more dynamic, you should avoid becoming a bottleneck for your team. Try not to take on critical tasks that have many dependencies or are on the critical path.

这里有一点很重要：随着你写代码的时间自然减少、注意力变得更加多变，你应当避免成为团队的瓶颈。尽量不要去接那些依赖众多、或处在关键路径上的任务。

Thinking time思考时间

This is something many tech leads tend to overlook: stepping away from the team and giving yourself some quiet time to reflect. Taking this time to think lets you step back, look at how things are going, spot gaps, and plan the team’s strategy moving forward. It’s one of those things that can save you from being blindsided when things go off track.

这是许多技术负责人容易忽视的一点：从团队中抽离出来，给自己一段安静的时间去反思。花时间思考，能让你退后一步，看看事情进展如何、发现缺口，并规划团队下一步的战略。这是那种能在事情脱轨时让你不至于措手不及的功夫之一。

For me, Friday afternoons became my go-to time for this. The week was winding down, the chaos was usually settling, and I’d use the time to review my notes, reflect on the week, and figure out what I might be missing. It was also the perfect moment to plan for the next week. This practice was a game-changer:

对我来说，周五下午成了我做这件事的固定时间。一周即将收尾，混乱通常也平息下来；我会利用这段时间回顾笔记、反思这一周，并想想自己可能漏掉了什么。这也是规划下一周的完美时机。这个做法彻底改变了我的工作状态：

— PDF p.28 —

it gave me clarity, helped me feel more in control, and stopped me from just getting swept up in the day-to-day flow.

它让我思路清晰，帮我更有掌控感，也让我不再只是被日常的洪流卷着走。

Of course, some days will be different than others. Some tech leads prefer saving days just for coding, while others might spend a full day planning. And then there are days when everything goes off track, and you’re just putting out fires. What’s important is that you’re aware of these various activities and ensure each gets the proper attention throughout the week.

当然，每一天都不尽相同。有些技术负责人喜欢专门留出整天用来写代码，另一些人可能花一整天做规划。还有些日子一切都脱了轨，你只是在四处救火。重要的是：你要意识到这些不同类型的工作，并确保一周之内每一类都得到应有的关注。

In conclusion, if you’re stepping into the role for the first time, expect to navigate ambiguity, resolve conflict, influence without authority, and spend as much time on communication as you do on code.

总而言之，如果你是第一次走上这个岗位，请做好准备：在模糊中摸索、化解冲突、在没有职权的情况下去影响他人，并且在沟通上花的时间和在代码上花的时间一样多。

Job titles may differ and responsibilities may be shuffled around, but the bottom line is:

头衔或许各不相同，职责也许被来回调动，但归根结底：

No matter how technical the tech lead role may look on paper, it is fundamentally about leading people.

无论技术负责人这个角色在纸面上看起来多么技术化，它本质上是关于带领人的。

I’ll be honest. I still find it hard to fully embrace this truth every single day. There are moments when I question myself, wondering if I’ve overstated the people part. But then I talk to another tech lead, about their daily challenges, their struggles, their people issues, and my conviction comes back again: unfortunately, I am right.

说句实话。我自己至今仍觉得，要每天都全然接受这个真相并不容易。有些时候我也会自我怀疑，琢磨自己是不是把“人”这一部分夸大了。但随后我和另一位技术负责人聊起他们日常的挑战、他们的挣扎、他们那些与人有关的麻烦，我的信念又回来了：很遗憾，我是对的。

Even if some people don’t want to hear it. Even if it’s hard to accept.

哪怕有些人不愿听到这话。哪怕它很难接受。

And maybe that’s part of the problem. If we were more up-front about just how much people leadership is required to succeed in this role, there would be far less confusion, and far fewer tech leads left wondering why the job feels so hard.

而这或许正是问题的一部分。如果我们早一点坦白：要在这个角色上取得成功，需要多少“带人”的功夫，那么困惑会少得多，也会少得多的技术负责人纳闷这份工作为什么如此艰难。

Because most of the struggle comes from underestimating this part of the work.

因为大多数的艰难，都源于低估了工作中的这一部分。

Understanding the Expectations of Your Role理解对你角色的期望

— PDF p.29 —

With so many assumptions about what the tech lead role involves, ranging from being the most technical person on the team to focusing entirely on people and processes, it’s impossible to meet every expectation. Some view the role as highly hands-on, expecting the tech lead to contribute code daily and make all the decisions. Others view it as a facilitator’s role, focused on guiding processes, supporting the team, and encouraging collaboration.

关于技术负责人究竟要做什么，外界有如此多的预设——从“团队里技术最强的人”到“完全聚焦于人与流程”——你不可能满足每一种期望。有人把这个角色看得高度亲力亲为，期待技术负责人每天都写代码、包揽所有决策；另一些人则把它看作一个使能者的角色，聚焦于引导流程、支持团队、鼓励协作。

The key to being effective is understanding your specific context, including your company, team, and stakeholders, and what they expect from you. This clarity will help you define your priorities as a tech lead and focus on what truly matters in your environment.

要做到高效，关键在于理解你所处的具体情境——包括你的公司、团队和利益相关方——以及他们对你的期望是什么。这种清晰，会帮你界定作为技术负责人的优先级，把精力聚焦到你环境中真正重要的事情上。

Read the Job Description阅读岗位说明书

Most tech leads I talk to have never read the official company job description for their role. They just made their own assumptions about what is expected of them. No surprise they often ended up in conversations with their managers on how they “are not focusing on the right thing.”

我聊过的大多数技术负责人，从来没有读过公司官方为这个岗位写的岗位说明书。他们只是凭着自己的假设，去猜公司对自己的期望是什么。难怪他们最后常常和经理谈成这样：“你没有把精力放在对的事情上。”

So, your first task when jumping into the tech lead role is to read the job description and understand what the people around you expect from you.

所以，当你走上技术负责人岗位时，第一件事就是去读岗位说明书，弄清楚你身边的人对你的期望。

Reflect on What Applies to You and How思考哪些适用于你、又该如何适用

Job descriptions for tech lead roles are often vague, filled with phrases like adaptability and openness to new ideas, grow team members, or come up with innovative solutions. While these may sound inspiring, they leave a lot open to interpretation. To make these expectations meaningful, take the time to reflect on how they apply to your day-to-day work and the current stage of your team.

技术负责人的岗位说明书往往写得很笼统，满是诸如“适应力强、乐于接受新想法”“帮助团队成员成长”“提出创新解决方案”之类的话。这些话听着让人振奋，但却留下了大量解读空间。要让这些期望真正有意义，你得花时间去思考：它们如何落到你日常的工作中，又如何对应你团队当前所处的阶段。

Your gut feeling is not enough to assess whether you’re doing a good job as a tech lead. To truly understand your role and align with others, you need clarity and agreement from your team and stakeholders.

光凭你的直觉，不足以判断自己作为技术负责人是否干得不错。要真正理解你的角色并与他人对齐，你需要来自团队和利益相关方的清晰认知与共识。

Start by asking the right questions. In one-on-ones with team members, ask, “What do you expect from me as a tech lead?” Juniors might say they want mentoring, guidance, and technical expertise. Seniors, on the other hand, may expect alignment, support, and help in removing blockers. Both perspectives are important, so note their inputs and adapt your approach.

从问对问题开始。在与团队成员的一对一沟通中，问问：“作为技术负责人，你希望我为你做些什么？”初级工程师可能会说他们想要辅导、指导和技术专长；而资深工程师则可能期望对齐、支持，以及帮忙扫清障碍。两种视角都很重要，所以把他们的意见记下来，并据此调整你的做法。

Don’t stop with your team. Extend the conversation to other stakeholders like clients, product managers, or department leads. Ask them the same question and listen closely to their answers. They may highlight areas you hadn’t considered, like managing external dependencies, aligning with broader business goals, or improving communication across teams.

不要只停留在你的团队。把对话延伸到其他利益相关方——比如客户、产品经理或部门负责人。问他们同一个问题，并认真倾听他们的回答。他们可能会点出你从未考虑过的方面，比如管理外部依赖、与更宏观的业务目标对齐，或改善跨团队的沟通。

You can also make this process simpler by using a form to collect responses from multiple people at once. Adding prompts like “What’s one thing I can do to better support you?” or “What areas do you think I should focus on as a tech lead?” can help you get more specific and useful feedback.

你也可以用一份表单同时收集多人的反馈，让这个过程更简单。加上一些提示语，比如“我做哪一件事能更好地支持你？”或“作为技术负责人，你觉得我应该聚焦哪些方面？”，能帮你获得更具体、更有用的反馈。

— PDF p.30 —

Once you’ve gathered input, it’s time to synthesize these expectations and share them with your team and manager. Define what’s realistic and clarify what’s not. For example, if you’re expected to “come up with new product ideas that increase revenue,” but your focus for the next six months is migrating a monolith to microservices, make that clear. Similarly, if some team members expect you to code as much as they do, explain why that may not be feasible.

收集完意见之后，就该把这些期望综合起来，分享给你的团队和经理。界定哪些是现实的、把哪些不现实的说清楚。例如，如果有人期望你“提出能提升收入的新产品点子”，但你接下来半年的重点是把单体应用迁移到微服务，那就把这一点讲明白。同样，如果有些团队成员期望你像他们一样写那么多代码，那就解释一下为什么这未必可行。

The goal is to ensure everyone is aligned and understands your priorities. Setting clear expectations early on helps avoid misunderstandings, disappointment, and potential conflicts down the line.

目标是确保所有人都对齐，并理解你的优先级。尽早设定清晰的期望，有助于避免日后的误解、失望和潜在冲突。

What If There Is No Job Description?没有岗位说明书怎么办？

It’s rare, but it happens. I like to see this as an opportunity. If there’s no job description, create your own by applying the same principles:

这种情况很少见，但确实会发生。我倒愿意把它看作一个机会。如果没有岗位说明书，那就运用同样的原则，自己写一份：

  • Jot down what you think is expected from your role.把你认为这个角色应当承担的期望先草拟下来。
  • Ask your stakeholders and team members about their expectations.向你的利益相关方和团队成员询问他们的期望。
  • Compile all inputs into a document.把所有意见汇总成一份文档。
  • Share it with your manager and team to get agreement.把它分享给你的经理和团队，达成共识。

An added bonus: you can make this document visible across the company and ask for more input. It might just kick-start the creation of an official job description.

额外的好处是：你可以把这份文档在全公司范围内公开，并征求更多意见。它说不定还能顺势推动一份正式岗位说明书的诞生。

Is This Role a Good Fit for Me?这个角色适合我吗？

Deciding if the tech lead role is right for you is deeply personal and unique to your situation. No one can answer this question but you. Start by exploring what the role entails and how it aligns with your goals.

判断技术负责人这个角色是否适合你，是一件非常个人化的事，也取决于你的具体处境。这个问题除了你自己，没人能替你回答。先去了解这个角色究竟包含什么，以及它与你的目标是否契合。

Here are some activities that can help you decide:

下面这些活动可以帮你做决定：

  • Talk to other tech leads about their day-to-day experiences, and see how you feel about what they are sharing. Do you like what you hear?和其他技术负责人聊聊他们的日常经历，体会一下他们分享的内容带给你什么感受。你喜欢听到的这些吗？
  • Read through your company’s expectations for the role. Keep in mind that it varies by company, so explore which environment aligns with your own definition. Don’t let anyone fool you: no matter how technical the role looks on paper, there will always be a lot of “dealing with people” in the role.通读你公司对这个角色的期望。请记住，不同公司的情况各不相同，所以要去探寻哪种环境与你自己的定义相契合。别被任何人忽悠：无论这个角色在纸面上看起来多么技术化，里面永远有大量“与人打交道”的成分。
— PDF p.31 —
  • Get feedback. Ask people around you how they perceive your fit for the role and why. What strengths do they see that align with it? What might hold you back?去征求反馈。问问你身边的人：他们觉得你适不适合这个角色，为什么？他们看到你身上有哪些与之契合的优势？又有哪些可能拖你后腿？
  • Talk it over with someone objective. People often bring up this topic to me in coaching. Surprisingly, very often, after just an hour of deep diving into their reasoning and worries, they get clarity on wanting to pursue the role or not.和一个客观的人把这件事聊透。人们常常在辅导中向我提起这个话题。令人意外的是，往往只要深入剖析一小时他们的理由和顾虑，他们就能清楚自己到底想不想要这个角色。

This being said, the only way to really know is to try it out.

话虽如此，真正知道答案的唯一办法，就是亲自试一试。

Common Pathways to Becoming a Tech Lead成为技术负责人的常见路径

There are three main pathways that can lead you to a tech lead role. In this section, I’ll break them down one by one, sharing insights into how each works, the pros and cons, and how they might align with your own journey.

通往技术负责人岗位主要有三条路径。在这一节里，我会逐一拆解它们，分享每一条路径是怎么走的、各自的利弊，以及它们可能如何与你自己的旅程相契合。

Taking Over the Role on Your Current Team在现有团队接任

The tech lead of your team announces they’re leaving, and you realize this could be your chance. This is exactly how I became a tech lead at Thoughtworks. When my current tech lead announced he was rolling off the project, I immediately offered to step in. It felt like the natural next step for both me and my team, aligning perfectly with my long-term goals, and the timing was perfect.

你团队的技术负责人宣布要走了，你意识到这可能就是你的机会。我当初在 Thoughtworks 当上技术负责人，走的正是这条路。当当时的技术负责人宣布要从项目上撤出时，我立刻主动提出由我顶上。这对我和团队来说都像是顺理成章的下一步，与我的长期目标完美契合，时机也恰到好处。

I had already been preparing to jump into a leadership role for a while. I took part in multiple leadership trainings, and I was taking on more and more responsibilities in my current team and outside of the team that required leadership skills. I was leading big initiatives that involved direct and constant interaction with the clients, growing other people in the company, and becoming more and more visible inside and outside the company by speaking at different events.

其实我为走上领导岗位已经准备了一段时间。我参加过多次领导力培训，也在当前团队内外承担了越来越多需要领导力的责任。我主导过一些大型专项，需要与客户直接、持续地互动；我在公司里培养他人；我还通过在各种活动上演讲，让自己在公司内外的能见度越来越高。

Having been on the team for nearly two years, I was the person with the longest tenure on the team (I was in a consultancy environment, where people rotate teams way more often than in a product company), so I had the most context on our products and technical solutions. In addition, I was the most excited candidate and felt confident I could take on the role.

我在团队里已经待了近两年，是队里资历最老的人（我当时在咨询环境，那里的人轮换团队远比产品公司频繁），因此我对产品和技术方案掌握的上下文最多。此外，我也是最积极的候选人，并且有信心胜任这个角色。

Based on these reasons, it was no surprise when the leadership team said yes to my request, with the condition that I prepare for a smooth transition. Together with my current tech lead, we built a plan that allowed me to step into

基于这些理由，当领导团队同意我的请求、但要求我做好平稳交接时，我并不意外。我和当时的技术负责人一起制定了一个计划，让我能够逐步

— PDF p.32 —

the role gradually. I initially took on the position of secondary tech lead (the tech lead-in-training, preparing to take over), allowing me to get a feel for the responsibilities while still having support.

走上这个岗位。我一开始担任的是副技术负责人（secondary tech lead，即“受训中的技术负责人”，为接手做准备），这样我既能体会各项职责，又仍然有人支持。

Here’s how the transition played out over the two months before my tech lead rolled off the project.

下面是在我的技术负责人撤出项目之前那两个月里，交接是如何展开的。

We kicked things off by setting up a clear two-month timeline. I started attending meetings with stakeholders and other teams, shadowing my tech lead at first, then gradually taking over and leading them on my own. Each week, we held handover sessions where I got a behind-the-scenes look at the tasks my tech lead was handling and caught up on team initiatives I hadn’t been directly involved in before.

我们以设定一条清晰的两个月时间线作为开端。我开始参加与利益相关方和其他团队的会议，一开始是跟着我的技术负责人观摩，然后逐步接手、独立主持。每周我们都开交接会，让我了解技术负责人正在处理的任务背后的来龙去脉，并补上那些我此前没有直接参与的团队专项的背景。

I began stepping into decision-making conversations within the team, initially with my tech lead there to guide me. After each session, we’d debrief, and I’d get feedback on what to tweak or improve. I also took over the tough conversations (risks, delays in delivery) with the client, knowing my tech lead would step in if things got tricky. On the internal side, I started handling progress updates and addressing potential issues with stakeholders, again with my tech lead as a safety net if I needed backup.

我开始参与团队内部的决策讨论，一开始有我的技术负责人在场指导。每次讨论之后我们都会复盘，我会得到关于该调整或改进什么的反馈。我也接手了与客户之间那些艰难的对话（风险、交付延误），我知道如果事情变得棘手，我的技术负责人会出手兜底。在内部一侧，我开始负责进展同步、与利益相关方处理潜在问题；同样，如果我需要后援，我的技术负责人就是我的安全网。

Looking back, there’s one key area I would approach differently if given the chance: ensuring clear communication with the team during the leadership transition. Here’s what I wish had happened, and what I actually did:

回头看，如果有机会重来，有一个关键方面我会处理得不一样：在领导权交接期间，确保与团队的清晰沟通。下面是我希望发生的情况，以及我实际遇到的情况：

What I wish had happened我希望发生的情况

In retrospect, my plan should have included clear communication to the team from my tech lead or someone on the leadership team about the transition, explaining that I would be taking over the role, when it would happen, and outlining the plan for the transition.

事后看来，我的计划本应包含一次由我的技术负责人、或领导团队中某人面向团队做的清晰沟通，说明我将接任这个角色、何时接任，并讲清交接计划。

— PDF p.33 —

What happened实际发生的情况

When I transitioned into the tech lead role, there was no official communication from leadership to my team; only the stakeholders were informed. I assumed the team knew, as I became less involved in daily tasks and focused on the handover plan. After my tech lead left, I started leading meetings and setting up one-on-ones. This confused the team, making them feel like I was overstepping.

当我转入技术负责人岗位时，领导层并没有向我的团队做任何正式通知；只有利益相关方被告知了。我默认团队是知道的，因为我自己渐渐不再参与日常任务、而专注于交接计划。我的技术负责人离开后，我开始主持会议、安排一对一沟通。这让团队很困惑，觉得我好像越权了。

During a one-on-one, someone finally said, “So, you’re the tech lead now? I assumed, but no one confirmed.” That’s when I realized there had been a lack of clarity. I asked leadership to officially announce my new role, and once they did, along with an apology for the oversight, things fell into place.

在一次一对一沟通中，终于有人问出口：“这么说，你现在是技术负责人了？我是这么猜的，但没人正式确认过。”那一刻我才意识到，一直以来都存在着模糊不清。我请领导层正式宣布我的新角色；当他们照做了、并为这一疏漏道了歉之后，一切才各就各位。

This experience taught me the importance of clear communication. If you’re transitioning into a leadership role, ensure this step is part of the process. It saves confusion, builds trust, and sets the tone for your leadership journey.

这段经历让我明白了清晰沟通的重要性。如果你正转入一个领导岗位，请确保这一步被纳入流程之中。它能避免困惑、建立信任，并为你的领导之路定下基调。

And sometimes, it’s the other way around: your team might know, but stakeholders or other support functions may be left out. Even when a promotion is announced internally, it’s not always obvious across functions. That can lead to confusion about responsibilities, misalignment in collaboration, and delays in support. So, when planning your transition, think about everyone that needs to be in the loop and make sure they are informed.

有时候情况正好相反：你的团队知道了，但利益相关方或其他支持职能部门却被蒙在鼓里。即便一次晋升在内部宣布了，它也未必能清晰地传递到各个职能部门。这会导致职责上的困惑、协作上的错位，以及支持上的延迟。所以，在规划你的交接时，想清楚哪些人需要被纳入知情圈，并确保他们都被告知。

The benefits of this pathway are as follows: the transition process into the role becomes smoother since you’re already familiar with the team, the technology, and the product, and you have your current tech lead by your side to guide your first steps.

这条路径的好处在于：进入角色的交接过程会更顺畅，因为你已经熟悉团队、技术和产品，而且你现任的技术负责人还在身边，引导你迈出最初的几步。

The main downside of this approach is that your team members already know you as a fellow developer, and it can take time for them to start seeing you as a leader. I experienced this myself: because they knew me so well, it took longer for them to trust me in a leadership role. People became more hesitant to share everything with me, and at times, my authority wasn’t taken as seriously. However, these issues can be managed by setting clear expectations with the team and addressing any concerns early through honest conversations.

这种做法的主要缺点是：团队成员已经把你看作一个“并肩的开发”，他们需要时间才能开始把你当成领导者。我自己就经历过：正因为他们太了解我，他们花了更长时间才在领导岗位上信任我。人们变得更犹豫要不要把一切都向我敞开，有时我的权威也没被那么当回事。不过，这些问题是可以管理的：和团队设定清晰的期望，并通过坦诚的对话及早化解顾虑。

There’s also a variation of this situation that can be even trickier: when the outgoing tech lead doesn’t leave the team but instead moves into an individual contributor (IC) role. While this can be a healthy shift if managed well, it often creates confusion or even tension. The new tech lead may struggle to fully establish authority if the previous lead’s presence looms too large, especially if they continue contributing heavily or unintentionally undermine decisions. This inverted power dynamic can make it harder for the new lead to bring change, and requires strong alignment, communication, and mutual respect between the two.

还有一种更微妙的变体：离任的技术负责人并不离开团队，而是转成个人贡献者（IC）角色。如果处理得当，这可以是一次健康的转变；但它常常会制造困惑，甚至紧张关系。如果前任负责人的存在感过于强烈——尤其是当他们仍大量写代码、或无意间削弱新决策时——新技术负责人可能很难完全树立起权威。这种倒置的权力关系会让新负责人更难推动改变，需要两人之间有很强的对齐、沟通与相互尊重。

What I’d advise in this case is to sit down with the previous tech lead and align clearly on how you’ll move forward together. It can really make a difference if you ask this person to actively support you during the transition, even if your leadership style ends up being different from theirs. This alignment is ongoing work.

在这种情况下，我的建议是：坐下来和前任技术负责人谈清楚，就你们如何共同往前走达成明确一致。如果你请这个人在交接期间主动支持你，效果会大不一样——哪怕你的领导风格最终与他不同。这种对齐是一项持续不断的工作。

— PDF p.34 —

Overall, transitioning to being the lead of your current team remains one of the smoothest ways to step into the tech lead role.

总体而言，转而为自己现有团队担任负责人，仍是走上技术负责人岗位最顺畅的方式之一。

Taking Over the Role on Another Team到另一个团队接任

Sometimes, you spot the opportunity yourself. Maybe another team needs a tech lead, and you proactively put yourself forward. This could be because you feel ready to grow into the role or because you’re curious to go through the process and get feedback. You might also bring it up in a conversation with your manager, asking for their support. Taking this kind of initiative is already a sign of leadership, even before you formally step into the role.

有时候，机会是你自己发现的。也许另一个团队需要一位技术负责人，而你主动毛遂自荐。这可能是因为你觉得自己已经准备好成长为这个角色，也可能是因为你想走一遍这个流程、获得反馈。你也可能在与经理的对话中提起这件事，请求他的支持。这种主动，在你正式上任之前就已经是一种领导力的体现了。

Other times, the opportunity comes to you. For example, the tech lead of another team is leaving, and your manager asks you to step in because you’re the best fit based on your skills and experience. You accept the challenge.

另一些时候，机会是找上门来的。比如，另一个团队的技术负责人要走了，你的经理因为你基于技能和经验是最合适的人选，请你顶上。你接受了这个挑战。

To make the transition smoother, it often helps to jump in as soon as possible and have some overlap with the current tech lead. This gives you a chance to cocreate a transition plan, absorb context directly, and ease into the role gradually (like I did with my tech lead; more on this in the previous section, “Taking Over the Role on Your Current Team” on page 15). That said, overlap isn’t always possible, or even preferable in every situation.

为了让交接更顺畅，通常尽早切入、与现任技术负责人有一段重叠期会有帮助。这让你有机会共同制定交接计划、直接吸收上下文，并逐步适应角色（就像我和我的技术负责人那样；更多内容参见前一节第 15 页“在现有团队接任”）。话虽如此，重叠期并非总是可行，也并非在每种情境下都更可取。

In some cases, stepping in after the previous tech lead has fully left can actually create space for the team to open up more freely, reflect on what wasn’t working, and give you a chance to establish your own leadership approach right from the start. The absence of overlap can create a clean slate, but it also means you’ll have to work harder to reconstruct context and rebuild trust without that direct handover.

在有些情况下，等前任技术负责人完全离开后再接手，反而能给团队腾出空间，让他们更自由地敞开心扉、反思哪些地方行不通，也让你有机会从一开始就建立自己的领导方式。没有重叠期可以带来一张白纸，但也意味着你必须更努力地重建上下文、并在没有直接交接的情况下重建信任。

There’s no universal right answer here. Both approaches have trade-offs, and what works best will depend on the team’s dynamics, the outgoing lead’s leadership style, and how much change the team is ready for.

这里没有放之四海而皆准的答案。两种做法各有利弊，哪种最合适，取决于团队的氛围、离任负责人的领导风格，以及团队对变革的接受程度。

Transitioning to a leadership role in another team does come with a few extra challenges. Beyond just transitioning to tech lead, you also have to go through a full onboarding process with the new team. They’ve already established their own way of working, and as a new leader, you may face some friction as they adjust to you.

到另一个团队转任领导岗位，确实会带来一些额外的挑战。除了转为技术负责人之外，你还得和新团队一起走一遍完整的入职融入流程。他们已经建立了自己的工作方式，而作为新任领导，在他们适应你的过程中，你可能会遇到一些摩擦。

If overlap with the outgoing tech lead isn’t possible, the best approach you can take is to start by focusing on building relationships and gathering as much information as possible about the product and team dynamics before you start to rock the boat. Forming a few allies early on can help you access the knowledge you need and get a better sense of how the team operates.

如果无法与离任技术负责人重叠，你能采取的最佳做法是：先专注于建立关系、尽可能多地收集关于产品和团队氛围的信息，然后再开始“搅动局面”。早早地结交几位盟友，能帮你获取所需的知识，并更好地理解团队是如何运作的。

— PDF p.35 —

All this makes it a bit trickier than taking over a team you’re already familiar with, where you know the people, product, and technical solutions.

所有这些，让这条路比“接管一支你本就熟悉的团队”要稍显棘手——在后一种情况下，你了解那里的人、产品和技术方案。

The upside is you’re walking into a fresh start: new team, new people, new rules. This is a chance to define how you want to be seen as a leader right from the beginning.

好处在于，你走进的是一个全新的开始：新团队、新人、新规则。这是一个机会，让你从一开始就界定自己想被看作怎样的一位领导。

Building and Leading a Brand-New Team从零组建并带领一支全新团队

As your company grows, a new team is formed, and it needs a tech lead. Whether you’re asked to take on the role or you volunteer, you’re starting from scratch. Everything is new, for you and the team. This gives you a unique opportunity to shape the team’s culture, processes, and technical direction right from the start.

随着公司发展，一支新团队成立了，它需要一位技术负责人。无论是被指派还是你主动请缨，你都是从零开始。一切都是新的——对你、对团队都是如此。这给了你一个独一无二的机会，从一开始就塑造团队的文化、流程和技术方向。

Pros: Everything is new, not just for you but for everyone involved. This gives you the opportunity to start fresh, define your role as a leader, improve on your previous experiences, and bring people into the team that are aligned with the culture you want to create. Your team members are also likely to be more engaged and curious, eager to contribute and take initiative at this stage.

优点：一切都是新的——不仅对你，对所有相关的人都是。这让你有机会重新开始，定义自己作为领导的角色，在过往经验的基础上改进，并把那些与你想打造的文化相契合的人招进团队。在这个阶段，你的团队成员也更可能投入、更好奇，渴望贡献力量、主动行动。

Cons: Everything is new, and you don’t have someone on the team to guide your first steps.

缺点：一切都是新的，团队里也没有人能引导你迈出最初的几步。

There’s a model that can help make sense of this: the Tuckman model, also known as Tuckman’s stages of group development, outlines the typical phases teams go through as they form and mature. You can see all the stages illustrated in Figure 1-3.

有一个模型可以帮你理解这种情况：塔克曼模型（Tuckman model），又称塔克曼团队发展阶段模型，它勾勒了团队在组建和成熟过程中通常会经历的各个阶段。所有阶段如图 1-3 所示。

— PDF p.36 —

Every new joiner sends a team back to the forming phase, but for a brand-new team this phase comes with added complexity. You’re not just onboarding someone into an existing rhythm; you’re building that rhythm from scratch. In this setup, the early stages tend to be longer and more uncertain.

每一位新成员加入，都会把团队打回到“组建期”（forming）；但对一支全新团队来说，这个阶段还带着额外的复杂性。你不是在把某个人迎进一种既有的节奏里，而是在从零开始建造这种节奏。在这种情形下，早期阶段往往更长、也更不确定。

You might find yourself moving back and forth between forming, storming, and norming as the team evolves, experiments, and learns how to work together. These stages are rarely linear.

随着团队演进、试验、学习如何协作，你可能会发现自己在组建期、震荡期（storming）和规范期（norming）之间来回反复。这些阶段很少是线性推进的。

To start with, you’ll need to understand what your team will build, why it matters, and how you’ll go about it. This often involves aligning with stakeholders, exploring technical options, and finding your team’s purpose within the broader organization.

一开始，你需要弄清楚你的团队要构建什么、它为什么重要、以及你们打算怎么去做。这通常包括与利益相关方对齐、探索技术选型，以及在更大的组织中找到你团队的使命。

At the same time, you’ll need to start shaping the team’s culture and establishing ways of working. This can take anywhere from a few weeks to several months, depending on team size, past working relationships, organizational maturity, and how often you actually get to collaborate.

与此同时，你需要开始塑造团队文化、建立工作方式。这可能花上几周到几个月不等，取决于团队规模、过往的合作关系、组织成熟度，以及你们实际能协作的频率。

People also need time to get to know each other and find their rhythm. Even experienced engineers need space to build trust and learn how to collaborate effectively.

人也需要时间去彼此了解、找到默契。即便是经验丰富的工程师，也需要空间来建立信任、学会高效协作。

And as the team’s scope evolves, you may need to bring new people on board, adding another layer of transition and adjustment.

而随着团队的工作范围演变，你可能还需要引入新人，从而又加上一层过渡与调整。

These phases don’t happen one at a time. They overlap, repeat, and evolve. But knowing they exist helps you recognize where your team is and respond with more clarity, patience, and intention.

这些阶段并不是一个接一个单独出现的。它们相互重叠、反复出现、不断演进。但知道它们存在，能帮你认清你的团队正处在哪个阶段，并以更清醒、更耐心、更有意识的方式去回应。

Required Skills and Mindset Shifts所需技能与心态转变

As a tech lead, you’ll need more than just technical expertise or leadership skills; it’s about embracing a new way of thinking.

作为技术负责人，你需要的不只是技术专长或领导技能；更重要的是拥抱一种全新的思维方式。

In this section, I’ll first explore the technical skills you’ll need, focusing on the importance of understanding the software development lifecycle and how it shapes your team’s work. Then, I’ll dive into the leadership skills and mindset shifts that will help you empower your team, align with stakeholders, and adapt to the complexities of this role.

在这一节里，我会先探讨你所需的技术技能，重点说明理解软件开发生命周期的重要性，以及它如何塑造你团队的工作。然后，我会深入那些能帮你赋能团队、与利益相关方对齐、并适应这个角色复杂性的领导技能与心态转变。

Technical Skills技术技能

In the section “Defining the Scope” on page 3, I explain why having technical breadth as a tech lead often matters more than being an expert in every technology your team uses. Your goal is to ensure that your team collectively has the capabilities to meet the expectations of the work. Of course, this doesn’t mean

在第 3 页“界定职责范围”一节中，我解释了为什么对技术负责人而言，拥有技术广度往往比对团队所用每一项技术都成为专家更重要。你的目标是确保团队整体具备兑现工作期望的能力。当然，这并不意味着

— PDF p.37 —

you can skip technical knowledge entirely; you still need to understand enough to guide your team effectively.

你可以完全略过技术知识；你仍然需要理解得足够多，才能有效地引导团队。

Let’s start with an overview of all the different stages in your team’s development cycle. I’m a big fan of teams having autonomy over what they build, which is why I embrace the “you build it, you run it” methodology. This approach requires your team to handle every stage of the software development lifecycle (Figure 1-4), from planning and analysis to design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance.

我们先概览一下团队开发周期中的各个阶段。我非常推崇让团队对自己构建的东西拥有自主权，这也是为什么我信奉“你构建它，你运维它”（you build it, you run it）这一方法论。这种做法要求你的团队负责软件开发生命周期（图 1-4）的每一个阶段：从规划、分析，到设计、实现、测试、部署，再到运维。

When your team owns the full lifecycle, there’s no way around it: you need to understand your product at every stage. This requires a solid high-level understanding of the whole process:

当你的团队拥有完整的生命周期时，有一点无法回避：你需要在每一个阶段都理解你的产品。这要求你对整个流程有扎实的、高层次的理解：

Planning, analysis, and design规划、分析与设计

A big part of your role is planning and analysis. Planning includes prioritizing competing features, estimating effort (as frustrating as that may be), setting milestones, and contributing to roadmap and capacity planning. While you may not own all of these tasks outright, and the responsibility for getting them done is shared across the team, product managers, and stakeholders, you’re often expected to guide or influence the process. More on this in the section “Planning and Keeping a Project on Track” on page 291.

你角色的很大一部分是规划与分析。规划包括给相互竞争的功能排优先级、估算工作量（尽管这让人沮丧）、设定里程碑，以及为路线图和产能规划出力。虽然这些任务未必全由你独立负责，完成它们的责任由团队、产品经理和利益相关方共同分担，但大家通常期望你来引导或影响这个过程。更多内容参见第 291 页“规划并让项目走在正轨上”一节。

— PDF p.38 —

Analysis is about understanding what you’re building and why, long before any code is written. That could mean working directly with customers or collaborating closely with a product manager to understand requirements. It also involves balancing cross-functional concerns like accessibility, performance, security, and maintainability, as well as making smart build-versus-buy decisions.

分析则是在写任何代码之前很久，就弄清楚你在构建什么、以及为什么构建。这可能意味着直接与客户打交道，或与产品经理紧密合作以理解需求。它还涉及在跨职能的关注点之间取得平衡——比如可访问性、性能、安全性和可维护性——以及做出明智的“自研还是外购”决策。

Once those foundations are clear, design comes into play. For these early stages, skills like architecture design and understanding how services are designed and scaled are key. The system architecture your team chooses, whether it’s microservices, a monolithic structure, or a hybrid model, will have a significant impact on every phase of development. Knowing the benefits and trade-offs of different architectures enables you to guide your team in making informed decisions about scalability, performance, and maintainability.

一旦这些基础清晰了，设计就登场了。在这些早期阶段，架构设计能力、以及理解服务如何设计和如何扩展的能力，是关键。你团队选择的系统架构——无论微服务、单体结构还是混合模式——都会对开发的每一个阶段产生重大影响。了解不同架构的收益与取舍，能让你引导团队在可扩展性、性能和可维护性上做出有依据的决策。

For example, working with microservices architecture may require a deeper understanding of distributed systems, interservice communication, and how to manage dependencies. Meanwhile, monolithic architecture focuses on internal cohesion and the impact of changes on the entire system. As a tech lead, you should be comfortable discussing these trade-offs with both your team and product stakeholders.

举例来说，采用微服务架构可能需要你更深入地理解分布式系统、服务间通信，以及如何管理依赖。而单体架构则聚焦于内聚性，以及变更对整个系统的影响。作为技术负责人，你应当能自如地与团队和产品利益相关方讨论这些取舍。

Implementation实现

During the implementation phase, your focus shifts to development. Depending on your product and the problem your team is solving, you might need stronger backend development skills, such as working with APIs, backend frameworks, database interactions, or database management. For frontend-heavy projects, familiarity with modern frontend technologies, performance optimization, and how the UI interacts with the backend will be needed. You might even need both if your project is full-stack. Of course, you’ll also need to understand the programming languages your team uses daily to contribute meaningfully.

在实现阶段，你的重心转向开发。根据你的产品和团队正在解决的问题，你可能需要较强的后端开发技能，比如使用 API、后端框架、数据库交互或数据库管理。对于前端偏重的项目，则需要熟悉现代前端技术、性能优化，以及 UI 如何与后端交互。如果你的项目是全栈的，你甚至可能两者都需要。当然，你还需要理解团队日常使用的编程语言，才能做出有意义的贡献。

Testing测试

Quality is your responsibility. While you won’t write every test, you need to ensure proper strategies are in place (unit, integration, and end-to-end testing) and encourage a quality-first mindset. Testing isn’t just about catching bugs; it’s about avoiding regressions and keeping technical debt in check. You’ll also need to understand how your system interacts with others.

质量是你的责任。虽然你不会写下每一个测试用例，但你需要确保有恰当的策略到位（单元测试、集成测试和端到端测试），并鼓励“质量第一”的心态。测试不只是为了抓 bug；更是为了避免回归、把技术债控制住。你还需要理解你的系统如何与其他系统交互。

— PDF p.39 —

Techniques like contract testing and CFRs (cross-functional requirements) can help avoid ugly surprises when systems integrate (more on this in the section “Continuously Testing” on page 245 and the section “Defining and Managing Cross-Functional Requirements” on page 232).

像契约测试（contract testing）和 CFR（跨职能需求）这类技巧，能帮你在系统集成时避免难看的意外（更多内容参见第 245 页“持续测试”一节，以及第 232 页“定义与管理跨职能需求”一节）。

Deployment部署

Your team’s deployment process says a lot about its efficiency and reliability. You need to understand your deployment pipeline, the infrastructure involved, and which parts your team owns. Whether working with cloud services or on-premises solutions, you’ll need to troubleshoot slow delivery pipelines and ensure releases are smooth. Familiarity with concepts like CI/CD (continuous integration/continuous deployment or continuous delivery) is nonnegotiable these days for ensuring fast, automated releases and quick resolution of production issues.

一个团队的部署流程，很能说明它的效率和可靠性。你需要理解你们的部署流水线、所涉及的基础设施，以及团队负责其中哪些部分。无论使用云服务还是本地部署方案，你都需要排查缓慢的交付流水线、确保发布顺畅。如今，熟悉 CI/CD（持续集成/持续部署或持续交付）之类的概念是硬性要求——它关系到快速、自动化的发布，以及生产问题的快速解决。

Even if your company has a separate team handling deployment, you still need to understand the process at a high level. This knowledge helps you anticipate how deployment considerations might affect your product and ensures your team delivers a reliable solution.

即便你的公司有专门的团队负责部署，你仍然需要从高层次上理解这个流程。这种知识能帮你预判部署方面的考量会如何影响你的产品，并确保团队交付的是一个可靠的解决方案。

Maintenance运维与维护

Building the product is just the start; keeping it running is the real test. In my experience, maintenance often takes up at least half of a team’s time, and ironically, established products that require ongoing maintenance are usually the biggest revenue drivers. Poor decisions made earlier in development show up here, and fixing them can cost a fortune. Observability skills, including monitoring, troubleshooting, and debugging, are critical to ensure the system runs smoothly and your team isn’t flying blind. You can’t improve a system if you don’t know what’s wrong with it.

把产品构建出来只是开始；让它持续跑下去才是真正的考验。以我的经验，维护往往要占用团队至少一半的时间；而讽刺的是，那些需要持续维护的成熟产品，通常恰恰是最大的收入来源。早期开发中做出的糟糕决策会在这里集中显现，而修复它们可能代价高昂。可观测性技能——包括监控、排查和调试——对于确保系统平稳运行、让你的团队不在“盲飞”至关重要。如果你不知道系统哪里出了问题，你就无法改进它。

Even if your team doesn’t directly handle all these stages (e.g., there are separate quality assurance or deployment teams), understanding how they apply to your product is crucial. Too many teams focus solely on the implementation phase, which can cause serious problems. Every phase plays a role in the final result, and as a tech lead, you’re accountable for that. It doesn’t matter how good your code is if it takes three days to reach production. In some contexts, that might be normal, but in fast-moving teams, that kind of delay can become a serious bottleneck. As a tech lead, you’re accountable for the entire delivery process, not just the code.

即便你的团队并不直接处理所有这些阶段（比如有专门的质量保证或部署团队），理解它们如何作用于你的产品仍然至关重要。太多团队只盯着实现阶段，这会引发严重问题。每一个阶段都会对最终结果产生影响，而作为技术负责人，你要对这一切负责。如果你的代码再好，却要花三天才能上生产环境，那也没用。在某些环境下这也许正常，但在快速迭代的团队里，这种延迟会成为严重的瓶颈。作为技术负责人，你对整个交付流程负责，而不仅仅是代码。

— PDF p.40 —

This might feel overwhelming, but you don’t need to master all these skills up front. Much of the learning happens on the job, and different areas will demand focus depending on your project’s type and stage. Projects also vary; greenfield projects are about new architectures and innovation, brownfield projects involve navigating legacy systems, and scaling projects focus on reliability and performance.

这听起来可能让人喘不过气，但你并不需要一开始就精通所有这些技能。大部分学习是在工作中发生的，而且不同领域会根据你项目的类型和阶段而要求不同的专注。项目本身也各不相同：全新项目（greenfield）关乎新架构和创新，存量项目（brownfield）要在遗留系统中穿行，而扩容项目则聚焦于可靠性和性能。

No tech lead knows everything, and that’s fine. The key is to focus on what matters now and learn as you go. Work with your team to create growth opportunities. Run experiments, host hackathons, or set up learning days. Side projects can help, but I prefer learning on the job. If your current role doesn’t offer the chance to grow, you can propose a new project or even consider moving to one that aligns with your goals.

没有哪个技术负责人是万事通，这没关系。关键是聚焦于当下重要的事，边做边学。和你的团队一起创造成长机会：做实验、办黑客马拉松、设立学习日。副业项目会有帮助，但我更倾向于在工作中学习。如果你现在的岗位没有成长的机会，你可以提议一个新项目，甚至考虑转到一个与你目标相符的项目上。

Leadership Skills领导力技能

Most tech leads think they need only strong technical skills in order to be effective as tech leads. I definitely believed so, and I was quickly proven wrong once I stepped into the role because the challenges that I encountered daily required soft skills.

大多数技术负责人以为，只要技术过硬就能当好技术负责人。我当初也深信不疑；可一旦走上这个岗位，我很快就被证明错了，因为我每天遇到的挑战都需要软技能。

Here are some examples:

下面是几个例子：

Two developers fighting for hours over what JSON parsing library to use两位开发为该用哪个 JSON 解析库争了好几个小时

My first instinct, like most tech leads, was to dive into the technical options myself and pick the “best” solution. I definitely made this mistake early on. But over time, I learned to ask questions before jumping into action. By listening to both sides, I realized that, surprisingly, the conflict was not about the parsing library, but actually, these two people had a recurring underlying conflict between them, so they could not agree on pretty much anything. So, instead of diving into the JSON libraries, I helped them resolve their personal conflict.

和大多数技术负责人一样，我的第一反应是自己扎进各种技术选项里，挑出那个“最好”的方案。我早期确实犯过这个错。但随着时间推移，我学会了在动手之前先问问题。通过倾听双方，我惊讶地发现，冲突其实不在于解析库，而在于这两个人之间一直存在着某种深层矛盾，导致他们几乎在任何事情上都达不成一致。于是，我没有去研究 JSON 库，而是帮他们化解了私人之间的矛盾。

The team wasn’t addressing tech debt团队迟迟不去处理技术债

Despite having the knowledge, the time, and the product buy-in to tackle it, nothing was progressing. The root issue wasn’t a lack of technical capability but the absence of someone willing to take ownership and drive the process forward. As a tech lead, you could easily step in and take charge, but that’s not sustainable long term. The more effective solution is to enable and empower a senior team member to take on this responsibility and lead the initiative.

尽管团队既有知识、又有时间、产品方也支持去处理它，却毫无进展。根本问题不在于技术能力不足，而在于没有人愿意站出来牵头、推动这个流程往前走。作为技术负责人，你可以轻易地跳出来自己扛，但这从长期来看不可持续。更有效的做法是赋能一位资深团队成员，让他来承担这份责任、领导这个专项。

— PDF p.41 —

All these situations, along with countless others I’ve encountered or seen other tech leads face daily, have led me to the same conclusion:

所有这些情形，以及我亲身遇到、或看到其他技术负责人每天面对的无数类似情况，都让我得出同一个结论：

Most tech problems are people problems.

大多数技术问题，本质上都是人的问题。

And solving these people problems requires strong soft skills.

而要解决这些人的问题，就需要过硬的软技能。

I dive deep into all the soft skills you’ll need as a tech lead in the Soft Skills for Tech Leads O’Reilly online course and Chapters 3 through 7, but for now, know that there are seven soft skills every tech lead needs:

我在 O’Reilly 在线课程《Soft Skills for Tech Leads》以及本书第 3 到第 7 章中，会深入讲解技术负责人所需的全部软技能；但现在你只需知道，每位技术负责人都需要七项软技能：

Listening倾听

Focus on listening. Everything starts with listening more.

把注意力放在倾听上。一切都从多倾听开始。

Building relationships建立关系

Building strong relationships will help you set the foundation for collaboration, alignment, and commitment.

建立牢固的关系，会帮你为协作、对齐和投入打下基础。

Giving feedback给予反馈

Feedback is your best tool for growing your team members and yourself.

反馈是你培养团队成员、也培养自己的最佳工具。

Delegating委派

Delegation is the secret to effective leadership and team empowerment.

委派是有效领导和团队赋能的秘诀。

Facilitating引导（主持）

Facilitation will help you bring all voices to the table and help your team reach decisions collaboratively.

引导（facilitation）能帮你让所有声音都上桌，并帮助团队通过协作达成决策。

Resolving conflicts化解冲突

Disagreements are not only inevitable but are actually a sign of a healthy team: you just have to learn how to navigate them effectively.

分歧不仅不可避免，实际上还是一支健康团队的标志：你只需要学会如何有效地驾驭它们。

Mentoring and coaching辅导与训练

By making use of mentoring and coaching tools, you can help your team grow without telling them what to do.

通过运用辅导（mentoring）与训练（coaching）的方法，你可以在不直接指挥“该做什么”的情况下，帮助团队成长。

Investing in your soft skills is always a wise decision. They never become outdated and are universally applicable. After all, no matter how much tech develops, you will always have to work with people, so you might as well get better at it.

投资于你的软技能，永远是明智之举。它们永远不会过时，而且普遍适用。毕竟，无论技术发展到什么程度，你始终都要与人打交道，那还不如把这件事做得更好。

— PDF p.42 —

Mindset Changes心态转变

As a tech lead, you need to shift from an individual contributor mindset to a leadership mindset as your success is now directly tied to the success of your team, not just your individual performance. This transition involves three key mindset changes, as shown in Figure 1-5.

作为技术负责人，你需要从个人贡献者的心态转向领导者的心态，因为你现在的成功直接与团队的成功挂钩，而不再仅仅取决于你个人的表现。这一转变涉及三个关键的心态转变，如图 1-5 所示。

The first shift, from individual to team focus, means understanding the following ideas:

第一个转变，是从“聚焦个人”转向“聚焦团队”，这意味着要理解以下观念：

  • Your technical expertise is irrelevant if your team is constantly struggling.如果你的团队一直在挣扎，你的技术再精湛也毫无意义。
  • The number of tasks you complete doesn’t matter if your team isn’t delivering at the same pace.如果你的团队不能以同样的节奏交付，你自己完成了多少任务都不重要。
  • Finishing your tasks quickly doesn’t help if your team is slow to deliver.如果你的团队交付缓慢，你把自己的任务完成得再快也无济于事。
  • Your self-assessment of doing a great job as a tech lead is meaningless if your team disagrees.如果你团队并不这么认为，你对自己“当技术负责人当得很棒”的自我评价毫无意义。
  • Personal results don’t count if your team isn’t achieving success.如果你的团队没有取得成功，个人成绩就不算数。
— PDF p.43 —
  • How well you work on your own does not matter if you can’t collaborate with your team.如果你无法与团队协作，你独自干得多漂亮都无关紧要。
  • Talented team members alone aren’t enough if they can’t collaborate effectively.光有才华横溢的团队成员还不够，如果他们不能有效地协作。

As a tech lead, it’s about ensuring the whole team moves forward and succeeds together.

作为技术负责人，关键在于确保整个团队一起前进、共同成功。

Equally important is transitioning from coding-centric thinking to value-driven decisions. Being a tech lead isn’t about the amount of code you write but the value your team delivers. Instead of always pushing for the latest technology, prioritize what works best for your team goals and gains team buy-in. Before jumping into coding, ensure assumptions are clarified and strategies aligned. And instead of dismissing meetings as useless, challenge their purpose to make them more effective for everyone.

同样重要的，是从“以写代码为中心”的思维，转向“以价值为驱动”的决策。当技术负责人，不在于你写了多少代码，而在于你的团队交付了多少价值。不要总是追逐最新的技术，而要优先选择最契合团队目标、并能赢得团队认同的方案。在动手写代码之前，先确保假设被澄清、战略被对齐。与其把会议贬为无用，不如去质疑会议的目的，让它对每个人都更有效。

Then there’s the need to step into long-term planning. The decisions you make today will affect your team tomorrow, so you need to understand how to balance immediate tasks with the long-term health of the project. Decisions made for short-term gains should not come at the expense of long-term maintainability or technical debt.

再有，你需要迈进行长期规划。你今天做的决策会影响团队的明天，因此你需要懂得如何在眼前任务与项目的长期健康之间取得平衡。为短期收益做出的决策，不应当以牺牲长期可维护性、或放任技术债为代价。

Empowering others becomes a core principle. Instead of defaulting to “I’ll handle this,” shift to “How can I enable someone else to take ownership of this task?” as the first approach is not scalable. (More on this in Chapter 6.)

赋能他人成为一条核心原则。不要一上来就默认“这事我来处理”，而要转向“我怎样才能让别人来对这项任务负责？”因为前一种做法是不可扩展的。（更多内容见第 6 章。）

Last, letting go of control is essential. As an individual contributor, you had a clear focus: your tasks moved from To Do to Done, often with little interference. But as a tech lead, you’re juggling multiple team members’ progress and tackling issues that might not even be on the board. Trying to micromanage it all is a one-way ticket to burnout (trust me, I’ve been there). Learning to trust your team and step back is essential. For more insights, see the section “Avoiding the “Therapist” Trap” on page 51.

最后，学会放手至关重要。作为个人贡献者，你的焦点很清晰：你的任务从“待办”挪到“完成”，而且往往几乎不受打扰。但作为技术负责人，你要同时应付多位团队成员的进展，还要处理那些甚至根本不在看板上的问题。试图对一切都事无巨细地微观管理，是通向职业倦怠的单程票（相信我，我去过那里）。学会信任你的团队、往后退一步，至关重要。更多见解参见第 51 页“避免‘治疗师’陷阱”一节。

Tip

提示

To help with your mindset shift, write the following sentence down and keep it somewhere visible as a daily reminder: “As a tech lead, you are as successful as your team.”

为了帮你完成心态转变，把下面这句话写下来，放在看得见的地方作为每日提醒：“作为技术负责人，你的成功，取决于你的团队有多成功。”

— PDF p.44 —

Integrating AI into Your Team把 AI 融入你的团队

To write this section, I reached out to someone I deeply admire: Birgitta Böckeler, a former colleague of mine at Thoughtworks and a true thought leader in this space. Birgitta is a distinguished engineer and currently serves as a subject matter expert and developer advocate for AI-assisted software delivery at Thoughtworks. With over 20 years of experience as a software developer, architect, and technical leader, she brings not only deep technical expertise but also a strong focus on how teams actually work and deliver software together.

为了撰写这一节，我联系了一位我非常敬佩的人：Birgitta Böckeler，她是我在 Thoughtworks 的前同事，也是这个领域真正的思想领袖。Birgitta 是一位杰出工程师，目前在 Thoughtworks 担任 AI 辅助软件交付方向的主题专家与开发者布道师。作为软件开发者、架构师和技术负责人，她拥有超过 20 年的经验，不仅带来深厚的技术专长，还非常关注团队究竟是如何协作、如何共同交付软件的。

Birgitta has been at the forefront of exploring how generative AI impacts software delivery, advocating for responsible experimentation and practical adoption strategies. Her writing and talks offer clarity, realism, and excitement in a field that often gets clouded by hype. I’m incredibly grateful she jumped in to help shape this section with her insights and recent work.

Birgitta 一直走在探索生成式 AI 如何影响软件交付的最前沿，倡导负责任地实验、务实地落地。在一个常常被炒作笼罩的领域里，她的写作和演讲带来了清晰、现实与热忱。我非常感激她出手相助，用她的洞见和近期工作帮我塑造了这一节。

With her help, I’ve pulled together what I believe every tech lead should understand about AI’s role in software development today. Let’s jump in.

在她的帮助下，我整理出了我认为每位技术负责人都应当了解的、关于 AI 在当今软件开发中所扮演角色的内容。我们这就开始。

Note

说明

In this book, I often refer to “AI,” “GenAI,” and sometimes even “LLMs.” While these terms are sometimes used interchangeably in everyday conversations, they aren’t exactly the same. Artificial intelligence (AI) is a broad field that covers everything from rule-based systems to self-driving cars. Generative AI refers to models that create new content, including text, code, and images, based on patterns in data. And within GenAI, large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude are a specific kind of tool focused on working with language and reasoning over text. Most of the tools discussed here fall under this last category. So when I say “AI” in this book, I usually mean “GenAI,” and more specifically “LLMs.”

在本书中，我会经常提到“AI”“GenAI”，有时甚至是“LLM”。虽然这些词在日常对话中常常被混用，但它们并不完全相同。人工智能（AI）是一个广阔的领域，涵盖从基于规则的系统到自动驾驶汽车的一切。生成式 AI（GenAI）指的是那些基于数据中的模式来创造新内容（包括文本、代码和图像）的模型。而在GenAI 之中，像 ChatGPT、Gemini 或 Claude 这样的大语言模型（LLM），是一类专门处理语言、对文本进行推理的工具。本书讨论的大多数工具都属于这最后一类。所以当我在本书中说“AI”时，我通常指的是“GenAI”，更具体地说，是“LLM”。

AI is here. It’s been here for some time, but now, more than ever, it’s everywhere. We might not all be fans of the hype, and it’s OK to have mixed feelings about it. But one thing is clear: we can’t ignore it. AI is now part of our toolbox. It’s useful, it’s evolving rapidly, and it’s not going away.

AI 已经来了。它来了有一阵子了，但如今它比以往任何时候都更无处不在。我们未必都喜欢这场炒作，对它心情复杂也完全没关系。但有一点很清楚：我们无法忽视它。AI 如今已经是我们工具箱的一部分。它有用，它在飞速演进，它不会消失。

Embracing AI thoughtfully is becoming a leadership skill in itself. We need to understand its potential, its limitations, and how it can support the work our teams are doing. This includes considering ethical implications, impact on team dynamics, and long-term maintainability.

审慎地拥抱 AI，本身正在成为一种领导力技能。我们需要理解它的潜力、它的局限，以及它能如何支持团队正在做的工作。这包括考量伦理影响、对团队氛围的影响，以及长期可维护性。

Your team will look to you for guidance on how to use it, when to trust it, and when to push back. The challenge is not just learning the tools yourself but helping your team develop safe AI collaboration and good judgment.

你的团队会指望你给出指引：该怎么用它、什么时候可以信任它、什么时候应当质疑。挑战不仅在于你自己学会这些工具，更在于帮助你的团队养成安全的 AI 协作方式和良好的判断力。

— PDF p.45 —

Use AI for your own work把 AI 用在你自己的工作上

Start with your own workflow. Experiment with AI on small, low-risk tasks: generating release notes, cleaning up documentation, summarizing architecture decision records (ADRs), or turning rough notes into onboarding guides. Some teams go further and train models on their internal documentation so new joiners can ask onboarding questions in natural language. Even without that investment, you can use AI as a smarter search layer across your team’s existing documents and templates. By trying these applications firsthand, you gain the experience you need to guide others.

从你自己的工作流开始。在一些小而低风险的任务上试验 AI：生成发布说明、清理文档、总结架构决策记录（ADR），或把粗略的笔记整理成入职指南。有些团队走得更远，他们用内部文档训练模型，让新入职者能用自然语言提问入职相关的问题。即便不做那样的投入，你也可以把 AI 当作一个更智能的搜索层，覆盖团队现有的文档和模板。通过亲身体验这些应用，你就能获得引导他人所需的经验。

Help the team use AI effectively, creatively, and safely帮助团队有效、有创意且安全地使用 AI

Your leadership is less about being an AI expert and more about setting the culture. Create an environment where your team feels safe experimenting and trying out new tools but is also encouraged to be skeptical, questioning outputs and raising concerns. LLMs don’t “know” things; they generate plausible text. They can sound confident and still be wrong. Encourage your team to treat AI outputs like they would advice from an over-confident junior developer: useful but never unquestioned.

你的领导力，与其说在于做一个 AI 专家，不如说在于塑造文化。营造一种环境：让团队可以安心实验、尝试新工具，同时又被鼓励保持怀疑——质疑输出、提出顾虑。LLM 并不“知道”什么；它只是生成貌似合理的文本。它可以听起来很自信，却仍然是错的。鼓励你的团队像对待一个过于自信的初级开发的建议那样对待 AI 的输出：有用，但绝不不加置疑地全盘接受。
