To help you help the team, you need to use AI coding assistants yourself to fully understand their strengths and pitfalls. That will enable you to teach your team when to use AI and when to avoid it. You can also ground conversations in context: What problem are we solving? What’s at stake if the output is wrong? Build safety nets with strong peer reviews, good test coverage, and knowledge sharing.

为了帮团队，你自己需要先用起来 AI 编程助手，彻底理解它们的长处与陷阱。这样你才能教会团队什么时候该用 AI、什么时候该避开它。你还可以把对话落到具体情境里：我们在解决什么问题？如果输出错了，会有什么利害？用扎实的同行评审、良好的测试覆盖和知识共享来构建安全网。

Regularly discuss as a team what worked, what didn’t, and where AI added value or noise. Social learning is key when it comes to AI.

团队要定期复盘：什么奏效了、什么没奏效、AI 在哪些地方带来了价值、又在哪些地方添了噪音。在 AI 这件事上，社会化学习是关键。

Amplify your expert knowledge across the team with AI用 AI 把你的专业知识放大到整个团队

AI can help you increase your reach as a tech lead. You can curate conventions and rules that reinforce good coding practices and prevent common pitfalls. You can also codify recurring tasks into reusable prompts, including threat modeling, improving ADRs, and structuring requirements, so the AI assistants can amplify consistent approaches.

AI 可以帮你扩大作为技术负责人的影响力半径。你可以整理出规范和规则，用来强化良好的编码实践、防止常见陷阱。你还可以把重复性任务固化成可复用的提示词——包括威胁建模、改进 ADR、结构化需求——好让 AI 助手把一致的做法放大开来。

Beyond prompts and rules, think intentionally about the toolset and MCP (model context protocol) servers you put around the team’s AI agents: integrations with other knowledge systems that provide useful context, or secure access to environments for debugging and incident response help. Each of these elements can amplify good practices and increase the probability that AI gives

除了提示词和规则之外，还要有意识地为团队的 AI 智能体配套工具集和 MCP（模型上下文协议）服务器：与其他知识系统集成以提供有用上下文，或为调试和事件响应提供安全的环境访问。这些要素中的每一个，都能放大良好实践，并提高 AI 给出

— PDF p.46 —

you better results and assistance, but they still don’t replace critical review and ongoing validation.

更好结果和协助的概率；但它们仍然不能替代批判性审视和持续验证。

Understand how AI changes learning理解 AI 如何改变学习方式

The deeper shift is how AI changes the way we and our teams learn. Sometimes the best approach remains doing the work manually, because judgment is forged by wrestling with problems, not bypassing them. Critical thinking, which means questioning assumptions, weighing trade-offs, and understanding context, is more important than ever. Use AI to encourage good habits, like consistent testing or clearer documentation, but don’t let it erode the fundamentals. Guide your team to reflect on where AI helps, where it hinders, and what it teaches them along the way.

更深层的转变，是 AI 如何改变我们和团队学习的方式。有时候，最好的做法仍然是手工去做这件事，因为判断力是在与问题搏斗中锤炼出来的，而不是绕过问题。批判性思维——即质疑假设、权衡取舍、理解上下文——比以往任何时候都更重要。用 AI 去鼓励好习惯，比如坚持测试、写出更清晰的文档，但不要让它侵蚀基本功。引导你的团队去反思：AI 在哪些地方有帮助、在哪些地方有妨碍、又在这个过程中教会了他们什么。

Manage stakeholders’ expectations管理利益相关方的期望

AI adoption often tempts organizations to chase numbers: faster delivery, more output, reduced costs. Some executives even assume teams will become “50% faster” just by adding AI to their workflows. These expectations are dangerous. They create pressure to cut corners, skip tests, or compromise quality just to hit inflated targets.

采用 AI 常常会诱使组织去追逐数字：交付更快、产出更多、成本更低。有些高管甚至想当然地认为，只要在工作流里加上 AI，团队就能“快 50%”。这些期望是危险的。它们会制造压力，让人走捷径、跳过测试、或牺牲质量，只为达成那些被吹高的指标。

As a lead, your role is to push back against oversimplified metrics and broaden the conversation. Monitor where AI genuinely reduces friction or accelerates learning, but balance that against things like code quality, maintainability, debugging time, and team satisfaction.

作为负责人，你的职责是抵制那些过度简化的指标，并把讨论拓宽。关注 AI 究竟在哪些地方真正减少了摩擦、或加速了学习，但同时也要把它与代码质量、可维护性、调试时间和团队满意度等因素放在一起权衡。

Like any tool, the value of AI depends on how thoughtfully it’s used.

和任何工具一样，AI 的价值取决于它被使用得多有心、多审慎。

By setting realistic expectations and widening the definition of success, you protect your team from unrealistic pressure and ensure AI adoption strengthens your outcomes, not weakens them.

通过设定现实的期望、拓宽“成功”的定义，你就能保护团队免受不切实际的压力，并确保采用 AI 是增强了你们的成果，而不是削弱它们。

Tip

提示

For a further deep dive into the topic, I totally recommend following Birgitta Böckeler on LinkedIn. She’s constantly publishing insightful articles and sharing up-to-date, practical information on how AI impacts software delivery.

想在这个话题上更深入，我强烈推荐在 LinkedIn 上关注 Birgitta Böckeler。她一直在发表富有洞见的文章，分享关于 AI 如何影响软件交付的最新、最实用的信息。

Key Takeaway本章要点

The tech lead role can feel a bit vague, and that’s often what makes it so intimidating at first. You’re expected to lead, but the path isn’t always clear. In this chapter, I wanted to bring a bit more clarity and calm to that confusion.

技术负责人这个角色会让人觉得有点模糊，而这往往正是它一开始令人望而生畏的原因。大家期望你去领导，但这条路并不总是清晰。在本章里，我想为这份困惑带来多一点清晰、多一点从容。

— PDF p.47 —

We looked at what the role typically involves and how it can vary across different teams and companies. This ambiguity isn’t necessarily a bad thing. It gives you the freedom to shape the role around your strengths, your leadership style, and what your team actually needs.

我们看了这个角色通常包含什么，以及它在不同团队、不同公司之间会如何变化。这种模糊未必是坏事。它给了你自由，让你可以围绕自己的长处、自己的领导风格，以及团队真正的需要，去塑造这个角色。

There’s no one-size-fits-all version of being a tech lead, and that’s the beauty of it. You can define what success looks like for you, as long as your team’s needs stay at the center.

当技术负责人没有放之四海而皆准的版本，而这正是它的美妙之处。你可以自己定义“成功”对你意味着什么——只要始终把团队的需要放在中心。

If the role still feels a little daunting, that’s OK. It’s a big step, but you don’t have to have it all figured out on day one. Start small, stay curious, and keep experimenting. That’s how you grow into it. That’s how you lead.

如果这个角色依然让你觉得有点令人生畏，那也没关系。这是一大步，但你不必在第一天就把一切都想明白。从小处着手，保持好奇，不断尝试。你就是这样成长起来的。你就是这样带领大家的。
